transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-22 16:00 UTC; Duration: ~52 minutes; Recording: yes; Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (CISO - Novara), Tom Reynolds (Head of Platform), Priya Patel (Infra Engineer)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you blocking time. this is Maya from Redwood, joining with Diego. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Aisha Khan: Hi Maya, good thanks. we wanted to cover SOC 2 and ISO posture primarily, and go through how logs and key management would work, also curious about control mappings.
[00:15] Diego Alvarez: Great, thanks Aisha. quick agenda: SOC 2/ISO artifacts we can provide, trust center access, controls mapping template, SSO/RBAC, audit logs and retention/export, encryption and KMS, and deployment options for data residency. anything to add?
[00:25] Tom Reynolds: timeline and any prerequisites for Dedicated or Private deployments.
[00:28] Maya Chen: perfect, we'll cover that. quick note, transcription may not be perfect on some acronyms, sorry if names come through funny.
[00:35] Priya Patel: yeah no problem.

[02:10] Diego Alvarez: So starting with SOC 2 — we have a SOC 2 Type II report for the period ending 2025-06. we can share a redacted copy under NDA, and we also host artifacts in our Trust Center for customers with enterprise agreements. the Trust Center link will include the SOC 2 report, ISO 27001 certificate, penetration test summaries, and our security policy documents.
[02:27] Aisha Khan: Is the SOC 2 scoped to hosting and inference platform only, or does it include private deployment features? we need to map their controls for our vendor assessment.
[02:35] Diego Alvarez: good question. SOC 2 covers our hosted production environment and associated controls — availability, confidentiality, processing integrity. for Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) there is a controls delineation; we provide control mappings and guidance — some controls remain customer responsibility, e.g., network segmentation for VPC peering, customer-managed keys. we'll provide a controls mapping spreadsheet that shows which controls are handled by Redwood and which are customer-managed.
[02:56] Tom Reynolds: that mapping is critical for us. do you have an example?
[03:01] Maya Chen: yes we'll include a sample mapping. Diego, maybe call out the usual ones — RBAC, SSO, audit logs, encryption at rest, key mgmt?
[03:08] Diego Alvarez: sure — typical splits: identity and access management for Redwood console/API is covered by Redwood's controls for hosted customers, and we support SAML/SSO integrations and SCIM for provisioning; however, if you deploy in a Private VPC with customer-controlled identity, the customer is responsible for network ACLs and peering configuration. audit logs: we retain system audit logs for 90 days by default in hosted; enterprise customers can request extended retention or log export to their SIEM via our log-delivery pipeline.

[06:30] Aisha Khan: 90 days is short for healthcare. we typically need 1 year of immutable audit logs. is there an option to ship logs to our AWS account or a third-party SIEM?
[06:40] Diego Alvarez: yes — for regulated customers we support log streaming to a customer-owned S3 bucket or to a SIEM via secure delivery. we can also set up extended retention in our secure archive, and we support write-once storage patterns for auditability. we'll need to put the export job in the order but it's a standard enterprise add-on.
[06:58] Priya Patel: what about tamper evidence and integrity? are logs signed or checksummed?
[07:05] Diego Alvarez: logs are checksummed and we can provide hash manifests on request for a given period. for customers requiring stronger guarantees we recommend streaming to your own S3 with bucket policies and object lock enabled.

[09:10] Tom Reynolds: KMS — can we use our own KMS keys (customer-managed keys)? we want CMEK so that we control key rotation.
[09:18] Maya Chen: yes, we support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments. for hosted customers we offer a BYOK flow integrated with common cloud KMS providers. Diego?
[09:25] Diego Alvarez: correct — BYOK for hosted, and for Dedicated/Private you can bring your own KMS and we support HSM-backed keys. there is a control mapping our security team will share that outlines responsibilities for key lifecycle management and backups. please note that certain ephemeral caches (KV caches) are handled in memory and secured by the runtime, but persisted model artifacts are encrypted at rest.

[12:00] Aisha Khan: about ISO 27001 — do you have a certificate and scope? and is it audited by an accredited body?
[12:07] Diego Alvarez: yes, we have an ISO 27001 certificate covering our control plane and hosted inference services, audited by an accredited certification body. we'll share the certificate via Trust Center and include scope documentation.

[14:30] Priya Patel: network details — for Private deployment we need to know if you support VPC peering, private endpoints, and whether any traffic traverses public internet for management plane.
[14:39] Diego Alvarez: Private deploys can be deployed as a VPC-hosted stack with private endpoints. control plane connectivity can be configured over a private link or require customer-managed VPN/peering. we have a deployment option where the control plane stays in Redwood-managed network but we can set up a private link for API calls. in the on-prem package, nothing leaves the air-gapped environment unless you opt into telemetry.
[14:58] Tom Reynolds: and are there specific ports or IP ranges we need to allow?
[15:04] Maya Chen: yes, we'll share a network diagram with required IP ranges and ports — Diego will include that in the follow-up materials.

[18:45] Aisha Khan: can you walk us through SSO/roles? we need fine-grained RBAC and the ability to map roles to our internal groups.
[18:53] Diego Alvarez: our platform supports SAML 2.0 SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access controls. roles are hierarchical — org admin, team admin, developer, auditor. you can map SAML group assertions into Redwood roles. we also support attribute-based access for route-level permissions in the console. there is an audit trail for role changes and admin actions.
[19:25] Priya Patel: are API keys auditable and able to be scoped?
[19:29] Diego Alvarez: yes API keys are scoped to projects/routes and have metadata for owner and purpose. keys can be rotated via the API and disabled. we also support OAuth client credentials for ephemeral tokens.

[22:10] Maya Chen: regarding trust center — we'll create a read-only link for Novara's security team that includes SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), ISO cert, penetration test summaries, secure architecture guide, and the controls mapping CSV. access can be time-limited and requires SSO.
[22:23] Aisha Khan: will we be able to download raw evidence or is it just summary docs?
[22:28] Diego Alvarez: typically we provide redacted reports and control mappings. for deep audits we can coordinate an NDA and limited evidence exchange. full raw artifacts may require additional legal steps.

[25:00] Tom Reynolds: do you maintain an evidence list for the SOC controls we can reference? that speeds our attestation process.
[25:06] Diego Alvarez: yes, our controls mapping has a column for reference evidence — e.g., config snapshots, architectural diagrams, policy docs, and log extracts. we'll attach sample artifacts.

[28:40] Priya Patel: question on data residency — we operate primarily in us-east-1, can you guarantee data residency for inference requests and logs?
[28:48] Diego Alvarez: yes, you can pin workloads to a region. hosted customers can select region at project creation and all inference and logs stay in-region. for added guarantees we recommend Dedicated capacity in the region or Private deployment inside your VPC.

[31:15] Aisha Khan: incident response and breach notification — what are your SLAs and timelines?
[31:22] Maya Chen: we have an incident response playbook and notify customers within 72 hours for security incidents, with priority notification for incidents that affect confidentiality or availability at customer tier. there are escalation contacts and post-incident reports available.

[33:50] Tom Reynolds: do you provide continuous monitoring feeds or SOC alerts?
[33:56] Diego Alvarez: we have monitoring and alerting internally and can provide select telemetry via the Trust Center or push alerts to a webhook/SIEM. for Dedicated customers we can expose more telemetry and integrate with your monitoring pipeline.

[36:10] Priya Patel: one more on encryption in transit — TLS versions and mutual TLS support?
[36:15] Diego Alvarez: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 for all in-transit traffic; mutual TLS is supported for dedicated private endpoints and for inter-service communication in Private deployments.

[39:05] Aisha Khan: in the event we need to run an internal audit of Redwood as a vendor, who do we contact and what is the typical turnaround for evidence requests?
[39:12] Maya Chen: engage our security partnerships team via the Trust Center; standard evidence requests are handled within 7–10 business days once NDA is in place. we can accelerate for a premium SLA.

[42:00] Tom Reynolds: cost/ops question — if we choose Dedicated to satisfy residency and retention, what is the onboarding timeline?
[42:07] Diego Alvarez: for Dedicated, typical onboarding is 4–8 weeks depending on network complexity and provisioning. Private on-prem deployments add another 2–4 weeks. we'll include a project plan in follow-up.

[45:20] Priya Patel: any known gaps in your SOC 2 mapping that we typically push back on?
[45:26] Diego Alvarez: sometimes customers ask for longer log retention and more immutable storage. another area is control evidence for customer-managed keys — we document responsibilities but customers often want tighter contractual language. we'll work through contractual addenda as needed.

[48:30] Maya Chen: ok, quick recap of action items: Maya will share SOC2/ISO artifacts via Trust Center link and NDA; Diego will send controls mapping spreadsheet and network diagram; Priya to share Novara's network diagram and required controls list; schedule follow-up deep dive next week.
[48:50] Aisha Khan: that sounds good. also please include a sample contract addendum for CMEK and log retention.
[48:57] Maya Chen: will do.

[51:10] Tom Reynolds: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[51:15] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with materials and a calendar invite for the deep dive. bye.

[51:40] (recording ends)

Notes: transcript contains some auto-caption artifacts; proper nouns and acronyms may be imperfect. References shared during call: Trust Center link (to be provided), controls mapping spreadsheet (to be shared), sample network diagram (to be attached).
